solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Huge local inn manufactured mind-altering substance (12)

indicatorNotes.manufactured: something manufactured is made up from raw materials, so the letters are remade

annotation.surface: A vast village pub has been turned into a drug factory.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a sentence about a pub producing drugs, but 'Huge local inn' is simply the twelve letters to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A hallucinogen is a drug that alters perception and the mind.

entries.clue: Short set of maps welcoming worker in Georgian city (7)

indicatorNotes.Short: a word cut short loses its final letter
indicatorNotes.welcoming: one piece welcomes the other inside it

blocks.note: ATLAS, a set of maps, cut short to ATLA
the ant is the crossword's standard worker

annotation.surface: A pocket atlas gets a new employee somewhere in the Caucasus.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Georgian' tempts a solver toward Tbilisi or eighteenth-century England; it is the US state of Georgia.
annotation.definitionFit: Atlanta is the capital city of the US state of Georgia.

entries.clue: Not so much about feeble musical (3,10)

indicatorNotes.about: one word goes around the other

blocks.note: a miserable effort is a feeble one

annotation.surface: A mild put-down of a weak stage show.
annotation.walkthrough: The French title happens to contain an English word, so the English half of the wordplay slots straight into it; 'musical' looks like an adjective beside 'feeble' but is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Les Misérables is the long-running stage musical based on Victor Hugo's novel.

entries.clue: Restricted where mangy dog sleeps? (6)

blocks.note: a cur is a scruffy, low-bred dog
the question 'where … sleeps' asks for its bed
a bed is where one sleeps

annotation.surface: A question about where a scruffy dog would sleep.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the answer is being read as two words, a dog and its sleeping place, while the whole word means held back.
annotation.definitionFit: To curb is to restrain, so curbed means restricted.

entries.clue: Character to do duty again in wildlife sanctuary (6,7)

blocks.note: re-serve: to serve, or do duty, a second time

annotation.surface: Someone takes up duty once more at a wildlife park.
annotation.walkthrough: RESERVE is read as RE-SERVE, serving again, though in the answer it means a protected area.
annotation.definitionFit: A nature reserve is land set aside to protect wildlife.

entries.clue: Camp originally ghastly, useless looking after guests (5)

indicatorNotes.originally: the origin of each word is its first letter

blocks.note: first letters of Ghastly Useless Looking After Guests

annotation.surface: A review of a dreadful holiday camp with hopeless hosting.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a bad holiday camp; 'originally' applies to all five following words, not just 'ghastly'.
annotation.definitionFit: The Gulag was the Soviet system of forced-labour camps, and a gulag is one such camp.

entries.clue: Most inquisitive, having no afternoon rest, almost (7)

indicatorNotes.almost: almost the whole word: its last letter goes

blocks.note: SIESTA, an afternoon nap, without its last letter

annotation.surface: Someone who skips a nap in order to keep prying.
annotation.walkthrough: 'having' only joins the definition to the wordplay; NO + SIESTA minus its A gives the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the superlative: nosy means prying, so the superlative matches 'most inquisitive'.

entries.clue: Tiny mark reported in detailed plan (4)

indicatorNotes.reported: what is reported is heard, so we go by sound

blocks.note: a tiny mark is a speck, said aloud

annotation.surface: A small blot turns up on a blueprint.
annotation.walkthrough: SPEC is short for specification, a plan listing exact details.
annotation.definitionFit: A spec, short for specification, is a detailed description of what is to be made.

entries.clue: These Europeans couldn’t be further apart (5)

annotation.definition: These Europeans couldn’t be further apart

blocks.note: people from Poland, the reading the surface pushes
the setter's meaning: the North and South ends of the Earth's axis, as distant as two points can be

annotation.surface: A remark about two nationalities with nothing in common.
annotation.walkthrough: Poles are people from Poland, but the North and South Poles are as far apart as two places on Earth can be.
annotation.definitionFit: Poles are Europeans, and 'poles apart' means as different or distant as possible.

entries.clue: Shakes audibly and chatters, not quietly (7)

indicatorNotes.not: the letter for 'quietly' is not there

blocks.note: p = piano, quietly in music; removed

annotation.surface: Someone's teeth rattle and chatter from cold, loudly.
annotation.walkthrough: PRATTLES without its P leaves the answer. 'Audibly' belongs to the definition, not a sound-based instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Something that rattles shakes with a clattering noise.

entries.clue: Study exquisite pen (7)

blocks.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn

annotation.surface: A review of a lovely fountain pen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'pen' looks like a writing instrument; here it is the verb, to shut in.
annotation.definitionFit: The verb sense of pen: to shut animals in an enclosure, to hold within limits.

entries.clue: Nothing in urge to reform villain (5)

indicatorNotes.in: one piece goes inside the other
indicatorNotes.to reform: to re-form the letters is to arrange them anew

annotation.surface: A desire to reform a criminal comes to nothing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'reform' pretends to mean mending the villain's ways; it rearranges URGE, with O placed after the R.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both name a dishonest, unprincipled scoundrel.

entries.clue: Doctor Dread beginning to rub part of chest (6)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: the beginning of the word is its first letter

annotation.surface: A physician, fearful, starts massaging a patient's chest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'chest' suggests the body and a doctor's examination; it is a chest of drawers.
annotation.definitionFit: A drawer is one of the sliding compartments of a chest of drawers.

entries.clue: Last month, dire playing in tie-break (7)

blocks.note: DEC is the calendar abbreviation for December

annotation.surface: Last month's dreadful play in a tennis tie-break.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Last month' means the final month of the year, not the month just gone.
annotation.definitionFit: A decider is a game played to settle a tie.

entries.clue: Clever bishop, such a reverend (6)

blocks.note: B = bishop, as in chess notation
a bishop is styled the Right Reverend

annotation.surface: Praise for a clever clergyman.
annotation.walkthrough: In Britain a bishop's formal title is 'the Right Reverend', so 'such a reverend' refers back to the bishop and gives RIGHT.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from the image of a quick, shining mind.

entries.clue: Scowl from serious expert (7)

annotation.surface: A stern specialist frowns.
annotation.walkthrough: GRIM + ACE: an adjective and a noun combine into one word for a face.
annotation.definitionFit: A grimace is a twisted facial expression such as a scowl.

entries.clue: Hopelessly drunk as bachelor? Bingo! (6)

blocks.note: B = bachelor, as in degree abbreviations like BA
lotto is a numbers game like bingo

annotation.surface: A single man celebrating a stag night, and a shout of success at getting it right.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bingo!' reads as an exclamation of triumph; it is the game, of which lotto is another name. Blotto is British slang for very drunk.
annotation.definitionFit: Blotto is informal British slang for extremely drunk.

entries.clue: Charge by a Spanish holiday area (5)

annotation.surface: The price of a package holiday in Spain.
annotation.walkthrough: COSTA is the Spanish word for coast, used in names like the Costa del Sol, the Spanish holiday coasts popular with British tourists.
annotation.definitionFit: The Costas are Spain's coastal resort regions, such as the Costa Brava.

entries.clue: Group of players in small courtyard (5)

blocks.note: S = small, as on clothing labels
a quad (quadrangle) is a college courtyard

annotation.surface: A team gathered in a little yard.
annotation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link here, not a sign that one piece goes inside another.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from sport, where the pool of players a team is picked from carries this name.

entries.clue: Tells stories about a steamship for girls from Glasgow (7)

indicatorNotes.about: one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: to tell stories is to tell lies

annotation.surface: Someone spins yarns about a ship to entertain Scottish girls.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tells stories' means fibs, not tales; L + A SS + IES. Lassie is the Scottish word for a girl, hence Glasgow.
annotation.definitionFit: In Scotland a lassie is a girl or young woman.

entries.clue: Upset crime scene extends across house (4)

indicatorNotes.Upset: in a down clue, upset turns the letters upside down, so they read backwards
indicatorNotes.extends across: the answer stretches across the gap between two words

annotation.surface: A disturbing crime scene spreads over a whole house.
annotation.walkthrough: A semi is British shorthand for a semi-detached house, one sharing a wall with its neighbour.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: British shorthand for one kind of house, a pair joined by a shared wall.

entries.clue: Misgiving about extremely large jacket (7)

indicatorNotes.about: one piece goes around the other
indicatorNotes.extremely: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

annotation.surface: Doubts over an outsized jacket.
annotation.walkthrough: 'extremely large' looks like XL for clothing; it takes the two end letters, L and E, which sit inside DOUB…T.
annotation.definitionFit: A doublet is a close-fitting man's jacket worn from the 14th to 17th centuries.

entries.clue: Quantity of paper covering large field of study (5)

indicatorNotes.covering: one piece covers, going around, the other

blocks.note: a ream is 500 sheets of paper

annotation.surface: A stack of paper piled over a big field of research.
annotation.walkthrough: REA…M wraps around L.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: a kingdom extended to any domain of knowledge or activity, like the realm of science.

entries.clue: Again found communist is being screened (12)

blocks.note: something screened is covered, hidden from view

annotation.surface: A spy is uncovered again, a communist hidden behind a screen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'screened' suggests a film showing; here it means shielded, covered.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym split in two: the prefix gives 'again' and the past participle gives 'found'.
